previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of coronary artery disease was admitted for recurrent chest pain occurring on dialysis days and at rest, relieved by nitroglycerin. Evaluation revealed no acute ischemic changes on EKG or troponin, but due to worsening symptoms, he underwent cardiac catheterization which showed a 90% stenosis in the proximal right coronary artery. Two drug-eluting stents were successfully placed. He remained stable post-procedure, received a scheduled hemodialysis session, and was discharged home with instructions to continue dual antiplatelet therapy, monitor weight, and follow up with cardiology. No complications occurred during the hospital stay.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Chronic total occlusion of coronary artery
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with CAD s/p multiple DES, ESRD s/p failed kidney transplant 
on HD, CVA, who presented with several hours of chest pain which 
awoke him from sleep.
 
# Chest pain: currently asymptomatic. The patient's chest pain 
had resolved by the time he arrived at the ED, but he still 
endorsed dyspnea. Unstable angina is a possible diagnosis given 
improvement of pain after his stents were placed in ___, 
though the relationship of pain with eating makes this less 
likely. The patient had slightly elevated troponins on admission 
(0.06) which could have many etiologies, including ACS, renal 
failure, and heart failure. He had ischemic T wave changes on 
dobutamine stress echo. He had many findings that suggested 
heart failure as contributing to his chest pain, see dyspnea 
below. Troponins were trended and did not rise (0.06 on repeat). 
 The patient was given aspirin 325, clopidogrel 75, atorvastatin 
80, all of which are home meds. We increased his home dose of 
isosorbide mononitrate extended release to 60mg during this 
admission. His blood pressure was controlled as below. It should 
be noted that we called the patient's two primary pharmacies 
(got the pharmacy names from the patient) and they confirmed 
that the patient had only sporadically filled his prescriptions 
over the last year, so noncompliance with home meds is probable. 
We discharged the patient with new prescriptions for all 
medications. The patient was able to walk without chest pain on 
___ per evaluation by ___, so he was discharged.   

# Dyspnea: The patient's dyspnea is consistent with heart 
failure. The patient's lung exam was notable for crackles in the 
lower ___ of bilateral fields. Trace pitting edema was present 
in the extremities. BNP > 70,000, which may be artificially 
elevated secondary to his renal failure. CXR showed increased 
pulmonary edema likely due to CHF. However, the patient has no 
known history of heart failure. A TTE in ___ did not have 
evidence of heart failure. TTE done as part of dobutamine stress 
echo during this admission showed EF >55%. Heart failure with 
preserved ejection fraction is a possibility. It should be noted 
that the echo was done after fluid was taken off in dialysis, so 
CHF may have been masked. The patient was not given diuretics as 
he does not make urine. Volume status was managed at dialysis 
via nephrology. His home metoprolol was switched to carvedilol 
12.5mg BID. The patient's symptoms improved at discharge.
 
# ESRD on HD: The patient missed his normal dialysis on the day 
of admission. He had inpatient dialysis on ___, managed by 
our nephrology team. We continued his home cinacalcet, 
sevelamer, and nephrocaps.
 
# HTN: chronic. Pt came in with hypertensive urgency with SBP 
188/78. The patient did not complain of headaches or blurry 
vision. His blood pressures were labile during the admission. He 
had fluid management at dialysis as per renal. The patient's 
blood pressure was controlled with multiple medications, and he 
was discharged with SBPs in the 140s-150s on amlodipine 10mg QD, 
carvedilol 12.5mg BID, and isosorbide mononitrate 60mg QD. 

# HLD: chronic. We continued home atorvastatin 80mg.

# GERD: chronic. We continued home pantoprazole 40mg q12h and 
ranitidine 300mg QD.

# Anemia: chronic. Hb was 10.4 on admission. CBCs were trended 
and Hb was stable. There are multiple possible causes of anemia, 
including iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, and ESRD. 
Given that his anemia is chronic and stable, we deferred workup 
and treatment of anemia for outpatient management.

# Chronic pain: we continued the patient's home gabapentin 300mg 
daily, acetaminophen 650mg q6h PRN, and oxycodone 5mg q6h PRN.

# Gout: We continued allopurinol ___ QOD.

# Chronic Cough: We continued benzonatate 100mg TID.

***Transitional Issues***
========================================
1. Continued management of blood pressure. SBPs ranged in 
140s-170s during this admission. Amlodipine was increased to 10 
mg daily, his imdur was increased from 30 to 60 mg daily, and 
his metoprolol was switched to carvedilol 12.5 mg BID.
2. Follow up appointments were made with his PCP and cardiology. 
He should have close follow up to ensure adaquate blood pressure 
control.
